questions.prompt: You have listened to one single song by a new group, and a friend asks whether they are the best group of the year. You honestly cannot tell yet. Which reply fits best?

options.text: I'm absolutely certain that they are the best group of the year.
In my opinion, they are the best group of the year.
I think they are the best group of the year.
I'm not sure they are the best group of the year.

questions.explanation: "I'm (not) sure that…" is the formula for a judgement you cannot yet make, so after one single song the honest reply is "I'm not sure they are the best group of the year." — and "that" may be left out, as here. "I'm absolutely certain that they are the best group of the year." claims the very certainty you have just said you do not have, while "In my opinion, they are the best group of the year." and "I think they are the best group of the year." both deliver the verdict instead of suspending it.

questions.prompt: Which line from a singer's portrait is correct English?

options.text: She has won her first award in 2019.
She has won her first award three years ago.
She won her first award since 2019.
She won her first award three years ago.

questions.explanation: A finished past time kills the present perfect, and "three years ago" is as finished as a date, so only the simple past survives: She won her first award three years ago. "She has won her first award three years ago." and "She has won her first award in 2019." both hang a dated, finished time on the present perfect, and "She won her first award since 2019." puts a simple past after "since", which opens a period running up to now.

questions.prompt: After twenty years in the same bank, Mounir left his job and opened a small bookshop of his own. Which phrase names what he did?

options.text: earning a lot of money
starting a business
university studies
becoming famous

questions.explanation: Opening your own shop is exactly what starting a business means. "earning a lot of money" is about being paid a lot for your work, which the text never says about a small bookshop; "university studies" names the years of study after secondary school; and "becoming famous" means starting to be known by everybody.

questions.prompt: Complete both gaps: "I agree ___ my brother, and we both agree ___ one point: the press asks too many private questions."

options.text: on ... on
on ... with
with ... on
with ... with

questions.explanation: You agree with a person and you agree on a subject, so the pair is with ... on: I agree with my brother, and we both agree on one point. "on ... on" treats a brother as a subject, "with ... with" treats a point as a person, and "on ... with" gets the two prepositions the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: Read this text: "Slim Ayari, a director from Tunis, wanted a documentary about the medina of Kairouan. Last spring he watched a short film on the internet and called the two brothers who made it: Sami Ben Kacem, who films weddings, and his younger brother Walid, who edits the pictures at home on the old computer their uncle Nabil gave them. He gave Walid two weeks to cut the first hour, and he paid Sami before the work even started. The film has been on television twice since June, and the brothers' telephone has not stopped ringing." In "He gave Walid two weeks to cut the first hour", who is "He"?

options.text: Slim Ayari, the director
Sami, the wedding filmmaker
Walid, the film editor
Nabil, the brothers' uncle

questions.explanation: The sentence itself removes two names: Walid receives the two weeks and Sami receives the money, so neither of them can be "He". The man who orders the work and pays for it is the one who called the two brothers in the sentence before: Slim Ayari, the director. Nabil appears only inside a clause about an old computer and never acts here.

questions.prompt: Read this text: "Sofiene Haddad writes the songs, and his cousin Amal sings them. For six years they have worked in the same small studio in Bizerte. Last spring a producer came from Tunis and offered Amal a contract for three albums. She signed it the same evening, but she added one condition: Sofiene's name goes on every record, next to her own, or there is no contract at all. She told the local paper that he has written every line she has ever sung." What does Amal's condition tell us about her?

options.text: She is loyal to her songwriter.
She is unhappy with her own voice.
She is afraid of the Tunis producer.
She wants to record without Sofiene.

questions.explanation: Amal signs a contract for three albums and then puts it all at risk so that her cousin's name appears next to hers, and she says in public that he wrote every line she sings: "She is loyal to her songwriter." "She is afraid of the Tunis producer." does not fit a singer who signs the same evening and sets her own condition, "She wants to record without Sofiene." says the opposite of that condition, and "She is unhappy with her own voice." is never suggested, since the text praises what he writes, not what she sings.
